messages:
maya: quick sync: I'm refining the admission design — comparing a per-tenant credit-ledger (fine-grained accounting, reclaimable credits, explicit drains) vs a token-stream model (append-only tokens, simpler backpressure). want feedback on tradeoffs + a migration plan.

jon: high-level: ledger seems better for predictable tail latency and reclaiming unused headroom, but it's more stateful. token-stream is simpler to reason about for the initial scheduler and makes eviction cheaper.

sasha: telemetry concern: ledger means we need new metrics for 'reserved_credits' and 'stale_reservations' and a periodic sweep job. token stream -> easier metrics (ingested_tokens, tokens_in_flight) but harder to attribute per-tenant leftover tokens.

li: compatibility note: console + Optimize want per-tenant accounting (cost breakdowns). ledger maps directly to billing and console UX. token-stream would need an approximation layer.

maya: agree on billing. also thinking about late-join requests: with token-stream a late join that expects to coalesce may get poor latency because tokens already moved forward. ledger can hold small `pending_credit` entries that let late joins join micro-windows.

jon: implementation concerns: ledger needs atomic decrement/increment paths across admission and drain. we can implement per-GPU shard ledgers and a best-effort global reconciliation. example sketch:```proto
message CreditReservation {
  string tenant_id = 1;
  int32 credits = 2;
  int64 expiry_ts = 3;
}
```
This lets us expire stuck reservations.

maya: +1 for expiry. we should also expose a `reclaimable` boolean for fast eviction in overload.

sasha: eviction policy tradeoffs: with ledger we can reclaim deterministically but risk thrash if reclaim window too small. token-stream naturally degrades by dropping oldest tokens. Which failure mode is less bad? I think deterministic reclaim + hysteresis wins for SLOs.

jon: agree but ledger complexity increases cross-host synchronization. proposal: local ledgers per host, with periodic checkpointing to a central _soft_ aggregator. central aggregator used for billing and cross-host fairness adjustments, not for fast-path admission decisions.

li: migration idea: dual-run. start by treating token-stream as the source of truth; implement ledger write-ahead on admission (write to ledger but continue to admit from tokens). After 2 weeks of matching signals and a reconciliation job, flip to ledger-first admission. This reduces blast radius.

maya: nice. also plan for `late_join_hint` in the request proto to mark requests that should be eligible to join an in-flight microwindow. token-stream doesn't support it cleanly.

jon: race case: if a reclaim happens while a request is being materialized, we must ensure the KV-cache isn't evicted mid-kv-read. suggest a two-phase reclaim: mark -> wait-for-ack -> evict. this needs a tiny handshake in the runtime.

sasha: add metric `reclaim_mark_to_eviction_ms` to detect long-lived marks. also bump alert if >200ms.

maya: ops-bot: can you create a rollout issue with steps: dual-run, metrics dashboard (reserved_credits, stale_reservations, reclaim_latency), and a small canary in EU region?

ops-bot: created issue RW-ENG-6652: "Credit-ledger rollout (dual-run)" assigned to maya, jon, sasha; canary target: eu-central-1; checklist template added. :white_check_mark:

li: one more UX ask: expose a breakdown of reclaimed credits in the console so customers see why tokens were evicted. even a sampled log would help.

maya: noted. next steps: I'll draft a follow-up RFC with proto sketches, the dual-run plan, monitoring runbook, and the two-phase reclaim handshake. planning a 30-min sync tomorrow 10:30 PT. ping if you can't make it.

jon: will be there.

sasha: same.

li: same.

maya: thanks all.
